title: Cross-team reliability launchpad checklist — Nov 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, time-boxed launchpad checklist to coordinate cross-functional work for rolling SLOs and reliability guardrails into active feature teams. Intended audience: SREs, feature-engineering leads, product managers, oncall leads, and release engineering.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- 95% of targeted feature teams have SLOs defined, measured, and wired into the SRE dashboard by the end of the 6-week runway.
- Oncall runbooks and paging thresholds implemented for critical routes (error rate and P99 latency).
- Canary + automatic fallback enabled for at least 2 high-traffic models/routes.
- Clear handoff: ownership documented; rollback paths validated; incident playbooks attached to each service.

Scope (what's in / out):
- In: API request-serving paths for hosted API and Dedicated (model inferencing latency and error SLOs), per-route error budgets, alert rules, and oncall readiness.
- Out: billing pipelines, embedding accuracy metrics (handled by Optimize team), long-term governance (policy doc to follow after launch).

Guiding principles / constraints:
- Keep SLOs simple and actionable: one latency SLO and one availability SLO per critical surface.
- Prioritize routes by customer impact and traffic (top 20% by QPS will be first wave).
- Avoid new infra work that blocks rollout; prefer configuration and routing policies where possible.

Stakeholders and roles (quick map):
- Product: Priya Singh — defines customer-impact tiers and acceptance criteria.
- Feature engineering leads: owners per service — finalize SLO targets and remediate.
- SRE: Ava Chen (lead) — SLO templates, dashboards, runbook checks, incident drills.
- Release eng: Lucas Park — rollout orchestration and canary config.
- Observability: Marco Reyes — alert tuning, dashboarding, synthetic tests.
- Solutions/security: Jordan Patel — ensure compliance for Dedicated/Private routes.

Launch timeline (6-week runway, high level):
Week 0 (planning): stakeholder kickoff; pick initial 6 services; nominate owners and SMEs.
Week 1: SLO workshops with each feature team — pick metrics, targets, and measurement windows.
Week 2: Dashboards and alert rules created by Observability; runbooks skeletons drafted by SRE.
Week 3: Canary configs + synthetic tests; dry-run incident drill for first service.
Week 4: Fixes from drills; finalize automation (rollbacks, fallback to cheaper model variant).
Week 5: Gradual progression to remaining services; ramp alerts to production frequency.
Week 6: Final review; handoff to service owners; retro + acceptance criteria verification.

Concrete checklist (per-service) — copy this into each service ticket: 
- [ ] SLO definition documented (latency target, availability target, measurement window).
- [ ] Owner(s) assigned (primary and secondary oncall).
- [ ] Observability: dashboard with P50/P95/P99, error rate, request volume (synthetics in place).
- [ ] Alerting: paging thresholds and severity matrix created and reviewed.
- [ ] Runbook: recovery steps, rollback procedure, known mitigation knobs (e.g., routing to fallback model).
- [ ] Canary: rollout policy configured (+ automatic rollback threshold).
- [ ] Load test/synthetic: smoke and 95th percentile run passing.
- [ ] Post-rollout checklist: monitor error budget consumption for 72 hours.

SLO suggestions (examples):
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile tail latency < 280ms over 7-day window for "interactive" routes; swimlane per region.
- Availability SLO: successful requests >= 99.8% over 30-day window for critical routes (exclude planned maintenance).
Notes: these are starting points — teams should adjust targets based on customer impact and capacity.

Measuring & tooling notes:
- Use existing metrics prefix: infra.api.request.* (avoid ad-hoc metrics names).
- Synthetic checks: three geographic locations, 1m cadence, track both cold-start and warm latency.
- Dashboard panels: include error budget burn rate and projected exhaustion date.
- Alerting tiers: P0 (immediate page), P1 (oncall ping), P2 (ticket/Slack). Keep noise low: aim < 10 actionable alerts/day across SRE triage.

Runbook & drill plan (quick):
- Draft runbook by Week 2; SRE performs tabletop drill by Week 3 with service owner present.
- Drill outcomes: owner documents 1) what fixed the problem, 2) what automation is missing, 3) root cause hypothesis.
- Post-drill: assign remediation tasks (priority: automation to avoid manual routing changes).

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Alert fatigue from over-sensitive thresholds. Mitigation: tune with historical baselines; delay production paging until after 24h of observed baseline.
- Risk: Rollout blocked by infra quota or capacity. Mitigation: prebook burst capacity with infra team; fallback to lower-cost variant.
- Risk: Owner bandwidth; remediation: require two owners (primary + backup) and limit first wave to 6 services.

Decision log (notes to self):
- Prefer per-route SLOs rather than per-model where routes vary by latency characteristics.
- Exclude load-testing windows explicitly from SLO windows.
- Use 7-day window for latency and 30-day for availability for initial reporting cadence.

Action items (who does what next):
- Priya: finalize list of first-wave services and assign product impact tiers (due 2026-11-05).
- Marco: create dashboard template and push to shared library (due 2026-11-06).
- Lucas: prepare canary policy snippets and a rollback script (due 2026-11-09).
- Feature leads: book SLO workshop slots (Week 1) and draft initial SLOs (due 2026-11-12).
- Ava: schedule tabletop drills and create retro template (due 2026-11-10).

Notes / loose threads:
- Need quick lookup for model-variant compatibility — product team to provide mapping (PR: ENG-4102).
- Confirm KMS/HSM gating for Private deployments before enabling synthetic tests in customer VPCs (Jordan).
- Conversation in #sre-ops: remember to include retention cost estimate for 30-day window dashboards.

Acceptance criteria for "launch complete":
- Each service has SLOs documented, dashboards visible in SRE console, alerts firing into paging channel with noise < 10 actionable/night, and at least one successful canary with automated rollback validated.

Appendix: useful templates (copy/paste)
SLO doc template:
- SLO name: [service-route-latency]
- Metric: infra.api.request.latency_ms.p99
- Target: < 280ms
- Window: 7d
- Owner: [name + backup]

Runbook skeleton:
- Symptoms
- Immediate checks (logs, recent deploys, infra capacity)
- Quick mitigations (circuit to fallback, increase replicas, disable rate-limited features)
- Escalation path

Slack threads & refs: #sre-launchpad (thread: "Nov launchpad kickoff"), refer to confluence page above for longer-term governance.

---
Draft notes: still want to reduce the SLO surface by one (combine cold/warm metrics where possible). Keep feedback inline in this doc; we will convert to per-service tickets in Jira (SRE-892 is template).
